## Findings
- claim-1: The authors reported computational verification for bigrassmannian cases with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-6@L48-L52|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The requested regressions hold by vertical Pieri: \[ s_{(1,1)}s_{(1)}=s_{(2,1)}+s_{(1,1,1)},\qquad s_{(1,1)}s_{(2)}=s_{(3,1)}+s_{(2,1,1)}. \] Hence \(c_{(1,1),(1)}^{(3)}=0\) and \(c_{(1,1),(2)}^{(2,2)}=0\).
- claim-3: Using the accepted LR presentation of \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), a right-to-left row-reading LR-tableau enumerator and integral SNF calculation returned torsion-free quotients \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^d\) for all 90 rectangular instances in \(\{r\le5,q=n-r\le6\}\setminus\{r\le4,q\le5\}\). In each row below, entries are \(d\), with columns \(i=1,\ldots,q-1\) and rows \(j=1,\ldots,r-1\): \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} (r,q)&j& (d_i)_i\\ \hline (2,6)&1&(2,2,2,2,2)\\ \hline (3,6)&1&(3,3,3,3,2)\\ &2&(2,3,3,3,3)\\ \hline (4,6)&1&(4,4,4,3,2)\\ &2&(3,6,6,6,3)\\ &3&(2,3,4,4,4)\\ \hline (5,2)&1,2,3,4&(2)\\ \hline (5,3)&1&(3,2)\\ &2&(3,3)\\ &3&(3,3)\\ &4&(2,3)\\ \hline (5,4)&1&(4,3,2)\\ &2&(4,6,3)\\ &3&(3,6,4)\\ &4&(2,3,4)\\ \hline (5,5)&1&(5,4,3,2)\\ &2&(4,10,6,3)\\ &3&(3,6,10,4)\\ &4&(2,3,4,5)\\ \hline (5,6)&1&(5,5,4,3,2)\\ &2&(4,10,10,6,3)\\ &3&(3,6,10,10,4)\\ &4&(2,3,4,5,5) \end{array} \] Every displayed \(d\) equals \[ \binom{\min(q-i,r-j)+\min(i,j)}{\min(q-i,r-j)}. \] [artifact ce9dca58d3924029b4839d830f43cfe6514239f9a1025dc2f51a2e1c9bb3fedb]
- claim-4: For any tabulated instance, the accepted \(N=d\)-element Schur generating families are irredundant: their images span \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\), whereas \(N-1\) elements cannot span \(\mathbb Z^N\); graded Nakayama then implies that no generator can be deleted.
- claim-5: The retained sandbox artifact does not document a second independently implemented LR/SNF computation, nor Pieri-based verification of all 90 SNF outputs. Thus the requested independent reproduction of every finite result remains unverified.
## Strategy
- Use the accepted integral LR presentation for each bounded rectangular instance, enumerating LR tableaux by rows right-to-left.
- Prove that the restricted relations \(h_k s_\mu\) suffice: \(A_+\) is generated by \(h_1,\ldots,h_q\), since \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) and \(h_k=s_{(k)}=0\) for \(k>q\). Thus \(A_+J_v=\sum_{k=1}^q h_kJ_v\).
- Check all \(h_k s_\mu\) coefficients independently by horizontal Pieri, including the two required zero regressions.
- Independently certify every SNF result: for each relation matrix, use a second exact method to determine rank and exhibit a rank-sized minor of determinant \(\pm1\). This proves saturation of the relation lattice and hence torsion-freeness; compare all invariant factors instance-by-instance with the first computation.

## Gaps
- The retained computation has only one custom Smith-normal-form implementation; its free ranks and torsion-freeness are not independently reproduced.
- The reduction from all LR relations to the \(h_k s_\mu\) relations was not included in the prior artifact.
- No retained certificates give rational ranks or unimodular maximal minors for the 90 matrices.
- The 90 rectangular instances are not yet identified with all admissible \(v_{r,s,t,n}\)-cases.
- Any completed computation would remain a finite verification, not a proof of the general conjecture.

## Next
- Produce and retain a second exact rank/SNF computation or maximal-minor certificates for all 90 instances.
- Record the proof that \(A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)\) after box truncation.
- Verify the two regression coefficients both by Pieri and by the tableau enumerator.
- Only after independent agreement, conclude irredundance for the corresponding finite rectangular instances; keep the general and permutation-parameter claims unresolved.
